200.title: Poland’s Constitutional Crisis Deepens as President Returns to Warsaw Amid Court Confrontation
200.summary: Poland’s constitutional dispute escalated on Friday, 30 October, after the reported suspension of the country’s Constitutional Tribunal president prompted demonstrations in Warsaw and forced President Karol Nawrocki to abandon an official journey to Senegal.
200.body: Poland’s constitutional dispute escalated on Friday, 30 October, after the reported suspension of the country’s Constitutional Tribunal president prompted demonstrations in Warsaw and forced President Karol Nawrocki to abandon an official journey to Senegal. A decade-long dispute over the judiciary The origins of the confrontation date to 2015, when disagreements over judicial appointments developed into a wider struggle over the Constitutional Tribunal. As EU Today previously examined in its analysis of Poland’s constitutional confrontation , Nawrocki has also proposed preparing a new constitution by 2030, potentially reshaping the relationship between the presidency, parliament and government.

200.title: Polish president Nawrocki pushes his way into top court amid rule-of-law tussle
200.summary: News Politics Polish president Nawrocki pushes his way into top court amid rule-of-law tussle Karol Nawrocki made his way through protesters around midnight in the latest escalation of his conflict with Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
200.body: News Politics Polish president Nawrocki pushes his way into top court amid rule-of-law tussle Karol Nawrocki made his way through protesters around midnight in the latest escalation of his conflict with Prime Minister Donald Tusk. 6, 2026. | Ezra Acayan/Getty Images October 31, 2026 11:03 am CET By Wojciech Kość WARSAW — Polish President Karol Nawrocki forced his way into the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw shortly after midnight on Saturday, in the latest escalation of the rule-of-law tussle between the PiS-allied president and Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Advertisement Inside, Nawrocki told Korwin-Piotrowska and other judges that were recently elected by Tusk’s parliamentary majority: “You are not judges [of the Tribunal].” The confrontation marked a dramatic escalation in the struggle between Nawrocki and Tusk’s government over how to reverse judicial changes introduced under the former nationalist Law and Justice (PiS) government.

500.title: OPINION | When AI agents get access to enterprise systems, who is accountable?
500.summary: Why agents are different Three characteristics make AI agents particularly challenging to govern. ● Autonomous: Unlike fixed scripts that follow predefined steps, AI agents can determine how to complete a task within their configured capabilities and permissions.
500.body: Why agents are different Three characteristics make AI agents particularly challenging to govern. ● Autonomous: Unlike fixed scripts that follow predefined steps, AI agents can determine how to complete a task within their configured capabilities and permissions. The same instruction may therefore lead to different sequences of actions. ● Privileged: Depending on their purpose, AI agents may require access to systems such as ERP, CRM, HR or finance. Building Accountability into AI Agents Accountability must be built into how AI agents are deployed and managed. Organisations should be able to answer the question, 'Who is responsible?' before granting an AI agent access to their enterprise systems, not after something goes wrong.

500.summary: In a groundbreaking demonstration of artificial intelligence in medical procedures, a biotech startup has successfully deployed an AI agent that autonomously performed brain surgery on a live mouse.
500.body: In a groundbreaking demonstration of artificial intelligence in medical procedures, a biotech startup has successfully deployed an AI agent that autonomously performed brain surgery on a live mouse. The AI system independently chose a gene therapy treatment and precisely injected it into the animal's brain, representing a notable advancement in autonomous medical intervention technology. The AI chose a specific gene therapy approach and then carried out the delicate task of injecting the treatment directly into the mouse's brain tissue. The successful gene therapy injection performed by an AI agent on a live mouse represents both a technological achievement and a prompt for careful consideration of how such systems should be developed, tested, and regulated in the future.

500.body: Biotech founder Gabriel Ocana Santero recently did that using an agent to successfully carry out a brain injection procedure on a living mouse. The team initially tested Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 model, but it refused to guide the needle into the mouse’s brain, suggesting it might stop midway through the surgery, which could endanger the animal. The team resolved the issue by using a separate AI agent on Opus 5 to make the necessary code changes, but they didn’t tell the agent that a live surgery was happening. And it’s far too soon to unleash an AI agent on a human brain.
